chapter: Carnegie Hall and the touring years
title: Visiting his mother in Saginaw and a failed foundry job
summary: He often missed his mother, who lived in Saginaw; he once took a foundry job but was too slow on the line.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So my mother/know I was comin' back so she knocked...I knocked on the door...surprised her...'cause she didn't know...she didn't see me too often 'cause I always on the road. In fact, I was on the road so much that when she...I went to meet her in Saginaw, Michigan...that where she was livin' at...my stepfather an' them was workin' at the foundry, makin' automobile motors. So I got together with them...went up in Michigan, an' we took off an' played all around Michigan. In fact, one time I got a job in a foundry. The man told me I was too little to work in the foundry, say I just be in the way, so I came on pitiful: "I need me a job. I wanta work."

So he give me a job workin' on an assembly line. Had to pull the wires outa the motors where the crankcase go. Well, I was so young and dumb, I guess, that I'd be in the way of all that [ ] They work by piece work so they was fast, and I was too slow, so most of the time I be standin' aroun'...lookin'...'cause that's why that they said I was too slow. They couldn't make no money with me holdin' 'em up. So I left there, went back into the music business again.
